pull: Two teams cleared 195, one team collapsed to 83, and nothing has traded.
desk: Week 1 is in the books and the board is louder than the scoreboard. C33DeezNutzz and Zygon both cleared 195, Hades9mm posted the third-best score of the week and spent $170 of FAAB like the sleeper puss woke up hungry, and StealingGas's Future Therapy Bills produced an 83-point crater and the worst-manager award.

Darkspaces spent like Jerry Jones, put Maye on the block, and still walked out 1-0. YesChef23 beat the Issue 1 #1. Four managers have listed players, no trade has cleared, and the desk is here for all of it.

hero.text: 195.82 with the full constellation: the highest score of the week, 44% over projection, and a win by fifty. Zygon matched the result at 195.70 in the same column, so call it a shared podium.
hero.desk: Two different paths to the same nuclear result.

zero.text: 83.32, the lowest score of the week, 36% under projection, and only 66% of a perfect lineup. Worst manager award. The RB committee is failing peer review in spectacular fashion.

prev_motw.note: Issue 1's Match of the Week: the commissioner drew the man who promised to be positive and kind. The desk went with the running backs. Swift did not care.

block.desk: Four listings in two days, each with a sales pitch worse than the last. Pitts was marketed as a player who fills the bench and never has to move.
London and Kittle are listed by the team that just scored the third-most points in the league. Either a plan or a dare.
Maye went on the block after a rough opener and the commissioner called it 'genius.' Deebo joined him a few hours later.

waivers.note: $301 for a running back, the biggest bid in the league. 'Will I regret it? Probably.' The commissioner priced his own answer.
$90 for Benson from the team that just posted the third-best score. The sleeper puss is awake and bidding.
$80 for a tight end, with Kittle on the block. The math works if you do not look at it.

desk.Darkspaces: Singleton for $301 on top of the earlier $101, so $402 gone before the first Monday night. He put Maye and Deebo on the block in the same week and still won. The desk would call it a pivot if anything pivoted.
desk.Hades9mm: Two bids, $170 combined, from the offense doing the winning. Buying and selling in the same week is a strategy or a mood.
desk.Zygon: No bids, and the IR Predictor still posted the co-best score of the week.
desk.Sarge71: No bids after a 0-1 start with a very good score. The desk respects the thrift.
desk.StealingGas: $2 spent and the roster is still churning. Four players on the block and 83.32 on the board.

post.desk: Living the injury-prone nickname, scoring 195, and winning by 70 is elite bit commitment.

drama.h: YesChef23 and Painty69, Now With a Result
drama.p: Painty69 dropped the L in rivalry week and admitted he does not have a clue what he is doing in this league. YesChef23 beat the Issue 1 #1 the same weekend. The bulletin-board material now writes itself.
drama.desk: The desk is not rehashing the Restaurant Arc. The desk is just noting that the receipts are timestamped.

drama.h: The Commissioner Does a Jerry Jones Bit
drama.p: Darkspaces told the chat the AI calls him the Jerry Jones of the league and he is here for it. Then he paid $301 for Singleton, listed Maye and Deebo Samuel, and trolled Painty69 for first-round picks after winning.
drama.desk: A commissioner who spends like there is no cap is a bit until the waiver wire reminds him there is.

drama.h: A Loud Board and Zero Trades
drama.p: StealingGas loaded Holani, Vele, Kyler and Pitts onto the block and begged the league to take the curse. Hades9mm listed London and Kittle. Nobody has bitten.
drama.desk: Four sellers and no buyers is a market in the same way that a locked door is an entrance.

drama.p: Zygon read the AI tag on his team name, noted that he also owns Walker and Mahomes, and posted the co-high score anyway. Darkspaces begged for no Chiefs injuries. The nickname is undefeated and unamused.
drama.desk: The nickname is profitable until the first training-room report. Then it is a prophecy.

trades.note: Nothing has cleared, everything has been listed, and the desk is tired of waiting. Two deals that fix real roster problems.

items.ay: Moves Maye while the block is hot and gets usable pieces back after burning $402 of FAAB.
items.by: Gets a young QB with upside and sheds one more piece of the science experiment that scored 83.
items.desk: It solves both problems on paper. Whether either side wants to solve problems is a different question.

items.t: The Please Take That Curse Special
items.ay: Finally offloads the player he literally asked the league to take.
items.by: Can afford a lottery ticket while the offense is rolling.
items.desk: One side is begging for the curse to leave. The other side can afford the lottery. This one feels closer to happening.

pre.ma: Start the highest-upside remaining piece and hope it finally produces. Do not rotate for the sake of rotating after 83.
pre.mb: Lock the proven volume. Sit any speculative flex that undercut the floor last week. Depth is the weapon.
pre.la: The RB room is a volatility bomb. One more quiet week and 0-2 starts looking structural.
pre.lb: A deep roster is only as good as the flex that did not get cute.
pre.edge: CMac91 is the clear favorite on paper and process. StealingGas needs a bounce-back or the therapy bills get higher.
pre.desk: The experiment continues. Peer review is watching. Closely.

pre.ma: Decide if Maye is still the franchise or if the block post was the signal. If starting him, go maximally aggressive with Swift and Collins.
pre.mb: Jefferson is non-negotiable. Stack the WR corps and let volume work. Avoid any low-floor flex.
pre.la: $98 of FAAB and a quarterback controversy of his own making. Margin for error is thin.
pre.lb: A solid win can make a lineup lazy.
pre.edge: Slight edge Snipe58. Darkspaces wins if Swift and Collins repeat, but the bankroll hit is already permanent.
pre.desk: The cap does not exist until the waiver wire reminds you it does.

pre.ma: Bijan and Montgomery are the engine. Start both. Do not sit proven volume after a strong loss.
pre.mb: Jeanty and Taylor are locked. The supporting cast that went quiet has to wake up or 0-2 becomes real.
pre.la: Both teams have stud RBs. The difference is which supporting cast shows up.
pre.lb: Both teams are one quiet receiver room away from 0-2.
pre.edge: Slight edge Sarge71 on recent production. fumbduckdumbfuck owns the higher long-term upside if the young core clicks.
pre.desk: A strong score and an L is the cruelest form of moral victory.

pre.ma: Lamar and Hurts are the identity. Start both and hope the skill players produce more than Week 1 volume.
pre.mb: Gibbs is non-negotiable. CMC and the rest of the backfield need to hit closer to projection.
pre.la: Johnny4Skins's dual-QB approach is safer but lower-upside.
pre.lb: Painty69's ceiling is the highest in this pairing if the backfield clicks.
pre.edge: Edge Painty69 on pure talent. Johnny4Skins can steal it if the dual-QB volume continues and Painty's pieces stay quiet again.
pre.desk: The war-crime backfield has one week of tape. The desk still believes in the crime.

pre.ma: JSN, McBride and the Coker spike were the Week 1 formula. Repeat it. The nickname can stay prophetic as long as the starters stay healthy.
pre.mb: Caleb Williams just dropped 37. Start him again. The rest of the roster needs the same aggressive mindset that produced the upset.
pre.la: Health is the landmine for Zygon, true to the name.
pre.lb: YesChef23's path is thinner if the QB magic cools.
pre.edge: Slight edge Zygon on cleaner skill-position production, but YesChef23 already proved the upset capability once.
pre.desk: Living by the training-room report is a lifestyle. This week tests it.

motw.ma: Ride Henry and Amon-Ra again. Start the supporting pieces that already proved the spike is real.
motw.mb: The Week 1 constellation is the blueprint. Do not get cute. Start the same group that just dropped 195.
motw.la: A rest or game-script overthink after a huge Week 1.
motw.lb: Any tinkering with the lineup that just posted the best score in the league.
motw.edge: The projection sits three points higher for C33DeezNutzz. The desk leans Hades9mm on floor and recent FAAB aggression.
motw.desk: Two teams that just announced themselves. Somebody's zero is about to get ruined again.
motw.stakes: Hades9mm built the third-best Week 1 score by hand and kept spending. C33DeezNutzz posted the highest score of the week on a lineup that beat its projection by 44%. Dynasty stakes: a Hades9mm win says the Henry stack and the FAAB aggression travel. A C33DeezNutzz win says the Allen constellation is the real top of the league, and the early-season showcase belongs to him.
sw: London and Kittle on the block
The same group has to hit again
A 44% overachievement is hard to repeat
motw.verdict: The numbers lean C33DeezNutzz, the desk leans Hades9mm. The sleeper puss is the more aggressive buyer and has the better floor. The constellation has the higher ceiling, and a ceiling is a nuclear option only when you are on the right side of it.

paras: Week 1 delivered what a 12-team dynasty is supposed to deliver: two nuclear scores, one complete collapse, a $301 FAAB swing, a trade-block manifesto, and the upset of the consensus top team. C33DeezNutzz, Zygon and Hades9mm announced themselves. StealingGas and fumbduckdumbfuck absorbed the early damage, and Darkspaces is playing with house money and almost no house left.

The rivalry between YesChef23 and Painty69 now has a result on the board, and the Hypothetical Trade Machine is open for business. A loaded block with zero completed trades does not last. Somebody is going to blink.
Next up: Hades9mm against C33DeezNutzz in the Match of the Week, Zygon against YesChef23, and the desk watching every thread into Week 2.
